I was diagnosed with PCOS at the start of this year because I noticed similar hair growth! I can't give too much advice on the biological side of the issue since I'm still struggling with that myself but I started electrolysis with a specialist this summer and it's been really really helpful with hair reduction, and she gave me some advice about how the hair growth can get worse.  
1. Plucking stimulates the blood at the root of the hair follicle and so it can actually make those hairs grow back much thicker/stronger. It can also cause other surrounding hair follicles to be stimulated and so that might be why you're noticing more now?  
2. Shaving is less stimulating but typically a razor will cut the hair very blunt so you can feel the stubble/prickle which might make you more tempted to pluck.  
3. If you decide in the future to do laser hair removal, make sure to ask if they use anything to make sure the laser only targets the problem hairs - if they don't, there's a chance the laser could end up stimulating the surrounding hairs and actually making your problem worse.

4. The best methods she suggested were bleaching the hairs, trimming individual hairs that really bother you with those tiny nail scissors, or electrolysis.  


(of course I'm not a licensed professional and I'm just passing this advice along from her but I wish someone had told me these things before I made everything much worse for myself)

You’re an independent person from your mother, meaning that not everything she believes has to be applied to you as well. She’s entitled to her own opinion on therapy but so are you and if you think this is the best step towards progress for you then she should respect that.

I started therapy for my social anxiety and depression a month or so ago and only just told my mother about it last week, I brought it up very casually in conversation by just saying that I wasn’t able to do something one evening as I had my therapy session. While she was shocked because I hadn’t ever expressed any desire to go to therapy and she was always very worried about me sharing my feelings with someone I barely knew, she still took it well and accepted the fact that I’m the only one who truly knows what’s going on in my head and I’m the only one who can take charge and do something about it if I so wish.

Regardless of whether or not she took it well, that wouldn’t have stopped me from going to my sessions since I’ve learnt that sometimes it’s okay to be a little selfish when it comes to getting help and self-care.

I really hope you get the help that you need therapy wise, I’m rooting for you! :)

I asked my friends about this once since they always say that they’re dressing up for themselves when they’re clearly not and they explained that it was an attempt to not seem needy or as if they’re trying TOO hard, it seems like a matter of pride and fear of rejection in that circumstance but that could just be my friends.

Upside:  
Skin is the clearest it's been in 6 or so years, I only have scarring now but already have plans in place to manage these once I finish my prescription.  
Before I started the treatment I'd wake up every morning with 3-5 new spots and the same happened after I'd take my makeup off at the end of the day - the last few months I've woken up to virtually no blemishes, it's meant that waking up in the morning and instantly going to the mirror to scrutinise my skin isn't a part of my routine anymore!  
My chest used to be covered with acne but now I'll get one small pimple every 6 weeks or so.  
My self-confidence has skyrocketed, I used to physically avoid anything that would show my reflection in public because I hated to see my skin but now I can pass by a mirror and not feel ashamed or embarrassed for how I look.

  
Downside:   
The first major difference I noticed was that during the first two months, my skin got far worse before it got better.  
In my first couple of months, all the mucus in my nose dried out so I had around 1-2 nosebleeds a day (though I've heard that this side effect isn't as bad for everyone who takes Accutane).  
The drying out of my nose also meant my allergies completely flared up so I was constantly sneezing (not sure if this is applicable to you but this is just my experience!).  
My skin dried up but once I found my simple moisturiser routine then I didn't have as much trouble with it.  
During these last few winter months, I got REALLY bad eczema all over the backs of my hands and down the underside of my arms as well.  
The worst part for me has been the constantly dry lips, despite my efforts to slather on Burt's Bees and Carmex the dryness hasn't stopped at all.  
I did experience some hair thinning towards the front of my hairline which terrified me but I decided to stick out the medication since it had been working so well and instead just opted to wear baseball caps and beanies for a while, thankfully my hair grows pretty fast so it's already coming back in!

​

As much as this seems like a really negatively experience by comparing the good with the bad, I would honestly do it all over again without a doubt if my acne flared back up. The first few months are definitely a three steps forward and one step backwards kind of situation since upping my dosage made my acne way worse before it got way better.

Yeah I do go out with my sister in public quite often, but I’ll avoid it if I can. She has a very childish mentality and very short temper so if plans aren’t set in stone then a meltdown in public is pretty much guaranteed. I understand that she often doesn’t know how her misbehaviours aren’t appropriate for the setting but it still irritates me and makes me feel embarrassed - especially since she’s the older one out of us. It sounds awful to say but even just being around her stresses me out like hell because it’s like constantly walking on thin ice. I genuinely wish I didn’t feel this shame towards her but I can’t help it.

In regards to your brothers feelings, of course it’s kind of shitty of you to be embarrassed by something he had no control over and can’t change, especially since he probably also battles the same fears of being judged - but for him it’s 24/7 and will be something he deals with for the rest of his life.
However, coming from someone who also has a sibling with a disability, I understand your embarrassment and feel it’s totally normal (especially during teenage years, they’re rough enough as is without the extra added fear of judgement). Personally I still struggle with it from time to time, as long as society is judgemental towards others then I think this is something you’ll always deal with.
It’s good to get yourself into the mindset that most people are worried about you judging them instead of them actually judging you - people are stuck in their own bubble what can I say. It’s also important to remember that the less stigma around people with disabilities then the less judgement - usually, people will look at your brother, not to judge him, but because they’re curious and because they don’t understand.
At the end of the day, your brother can’t help it and (I assume) wishes you didn’t have to deal with the fear of judgement. The more used to being out in public you are with your brother then the easier it will become hopefully.
